structured_output.title: Pickups and the action button
structured_output.summary: Track JSON gets an optional `pickups` list ({at, lateral}). Only Dust Bowl uses it: two rows of three mustard boxes on its straights, clear of the ramp run-out. If the player drives through a box while not armed, the box vanishes for 300 ticks and the player is armed. Firing with CarInput `action` (replay flag bit 2; Space or the ⌀64 lightning button above GAS) gives a 90-tick boost to a top speed of 32. AI cars never collect or fire. RaceView gets optional pickup and boost fields, present only on pickup tracks. The action button and the desktop SPACE · POWER-UP keycap appear only then, so tracks without pickups, replays, bot laps and current HUD tests are unchanged.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Track data takes an optional `pickups: {at, lateral}[]`. validateTrack accepts it and rejects `at` outside [0, 1) or |lateral| > width/2 − 1, naming the field. A track without the key validates to a copy without it. trackLayout(track).pickups gives one world {x, z} per pickup (empty without any). Dust Bowl declares ≥ 2 pickups; Bramble Bends and Hay Loop declare none.

On Dust Bowl, raceView racers[0] has `armed: false` and `boostTicks: 0`, and RaceView has `pickups` (one boolean per layout pickup, all true). After car 0's centre passes within 2.5 units of a pickup, armed is true and that entry is false. AI cars that drive through boxes leave them present and their racer views always show armed false.

Respawn: a collected pickup's `pickups` entry stays false for exactly 300 ticks, then is true again. An armed player who drives through another present box leaves it present (no stacking). Collecting alone never changes any car view compared with the same inputs on a copy of the track without pickups.

Boost: car 0 at full throttle on a Dust Bowl straight at 25 units/s, armed, gets one tick with `action: true`. armed turns false and boostTicks becomes 90, then counts down 1 per tick to 0. Speed goes above 25 during the boost and never above 32. Within 120 ticks after the boost ends it is at most 25.5. `action: true` while not armed changes nothing compared with the same run without it.

Tracks without pickups behave exactly as before: on Bramble Bends, running with `action: true` every tick gives car views and race views identical to the run without it. Those RaceViews have no `pickups` key and racer views have no `armed` or `boostTicks` keys.

Replays: `action: true` is stored as flag bit 2. encode→decode gives `action: true` back, and runReplay of a recorded Dust Bowl run with one fired boost reproduces the live run's final car views exactly. Decoded frames with bit 2 clear have no `action` key.

Input: Space sets `action: true` in the combined input's read() (it calls preventDefault). A Space press released before the next read still gives one read with `action: true`. A press on the action touch zone also counts. When neither is pressed, read() has no `action` key.

In the race UI, after syncing a RaceView whose player racer has an `armed` field, the touch layer gains a button named "Boost" with the lightning icon, sitting above GAS. It is aria-disabled="true" while not armed and enabled while armed. It is marked popping on the sync where armed turns true. With no `armed` field there is no Boost button and there are 4 touch zones.

On desktop, a race UI synced with a pickup RaceView shows the legend STEER, GAS, BRAKE, POWER-UP, PAUSE, with a SPACE keycap for POWER-UP. Without pickups it stays as it is. A registered stage renders the armed Boost button. On Dust Bowl the race scene has a 'pickups' group with one mesh per layout pickup, and a mesh hides while its `pickups` entry is false.

playtest.whatYoullSee: Dust Bowl now has mustard boxes on its straights. Drive through one and it vanishes, and the round lightning button above GAS turns mustard with a little pop. Tap it (or press Space on a computer) and the car surges ahead for a moment. Five seconds later the box is back. Bramble Bends and Hay Loop look and drive exactly as before, with no lightning button.
howToTest: Open the preview on your phone in landscape and tap RACE. That starts Bramble Bends: check there's no lightning button above GAS.
Finish the race and tap NEXT RACE to go to Dust Bowl.
After GO, check a dirt-coloured round lightning button sits above GAS, and mustard boxes are on the straights.
Drive through a box: it disappears and the lightning button turns mustard with a quick pop.
Tap the lightning button while holding GAS on a straight: the car should visibly speed up for about a second and a half, then settle back.
Drive past the same spot about five seconds later: the box is back.
On a computer at full screen, start Dust Bowl the same way. The bottom-left key legend should show a SPACE · POWER-UP key, and pressing Space after collecting a box gives the boost.
